messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed kv cache hit rate falling for a subset of long-context requests in prod :thinking:
maya: Grafana panel (shortlink) https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kvcache/long-contexts :eyes:
liam: Can you paste the prom query you're using? Might be a sampling artifact from the telemetry agent.
maya: Query is `sum(rate(kvcache_hits_total[1m])) / sum(rate(kvcache_lookups_total[1m]))` per model+shard. Seems legit but hit ratio is ~0.6 for >8k tokens vs ~0.9 for short chats.
sophia: Do we have kv residency histograms? I worry about fragmentation causing hot items to be evicted even though overall residency looks ok.
andrew: We emit `kvcache_residency_seconds_bucket` but only at sample_rate=0.01 currently. That low sample rate might be flattening spikes.
metrics-bot: metric alert: kvcache_evictions_total increased 3x on shard gpu-7 between 1971999000 and 1972000200.
kai: Quick idea: increase sample_rate to 0.1 for affected shards for 1h and capture full histograms. Overhead should be ~2-3% on exporter CPU.
liam: +1 to temp bump. Also suggest adding an eviction_reason tag (age|frag|oom) — right now evictions are opaque which makes root cause hard.
sophia: Agree. Fragmentation detection could be: evictions where residency < X and frag_ratio > 0.6. Need a derived metric.
maya: I sketched a prom recording rule:
```
kvcache_evictions_by_reason = sum by (shard,reason) (
  increase(kvcache_evictions_total{reason!=""}[5m])
)
```
But we don't currently set `reason` label in runtime.
andrew: Runtime change is small: set label from eviction path (age/frag/oom). Will push change to canary runtime tomorrow.
liam: For dashboards we should avoid high-cardinality labels across models. Keep reason and shard, but drop prompt_id/trace_id. Use model_family where possible.
kai: Also propose an event stream for long-context sessions: emit session_id + residency_sample every 5m. Put those in a separate timeseries store (not Prom) to inspect sequences.
sophia: That helps reproduce memory growth patterns. Long chats sometimes show slow gradual growth in KV residency — could be a leak or never-referenced fragments.
maya: On canary run with higher sample rate: initial results look like fragmentation spikes after attention recompute at ~6k tokens. Evictions are dominated by small-frag evictions, not age-based.
liam: Action items: (1) andrew to roll reason label + deploy; (2) kai to spin short-term higher sampling job and store session traces; (3) maya to update grafana panels to show eviction_reason and frag_ratio; (4) sophia to add alert for frag_ratio > 0.7 with evictions rising.
andrew: Rolling reason label to canary now. Will report logs. deploy-bot: deploy started for runtime/canary-eviction-reasons @1972001500
metrics-bot: note: increase in scrape cardinality expected while sampling bumped; alerts may fire — silencing infra-alerts for 1h.
maya: Thanks — will monitor panels and post back findings.
liam: If fragmentation is root cause we should consider compact-on-eviction or a small background compactor job. Tradeoff CPU vs memory stability.
sophia: Yep. Keep the compactor opt-in per-customer for Dedicated/Private. Need perf numbers first.
maya: Closing loop later today with numbers. :thumbsup:
